channel.title: The Epoch Institute — What's new
channel.description: What the Institute has added and changed.

item.title: Twelve more religions and sixteen more languages
item.guid: 2026-11-03 Twelve more religions and sixteen more languages
item.description: Twelve religions with their spread on the faith maps: the religions of Mesopotamia, Canaan, Rome and the Celts, Slavic paganism and Mithraism, Tengrism, Bon and Chinese folk religion, and the Druze faith, Yazidism and Haitian Vodou. And sixteen languages: Pali, Tamil, Malay, Mongolian, Armenian, Georgian, Middle Persian, Ottoman Turkish, Old English, Gothic, Old Church Slavonic, Phoenician, Coptic, Ge'ez, Guarani and Hawaiian.

item.title: Twenty more cultures
item.description: Profiles of twenty more peoples and cultures without a state of their own: living peoples (the San, Khoekhoe and Tuareg, the Inuit, Navajo, Lakota and Kalinago, and Aboriginal Australians) and the cultures known from archaeology, from the Clovis and Paracas cultures to La Tène, Hallstatt, Cucuteni–Trypillia, the Nuragic civilisation and the Iberians, and in Asia the Tocharians, Longshan, Hongshan, Erlitou and the Hoabinhian.

item.title: Eighty-one more state profiles
item.description: Full profiles, with power curves, key facts, section pictures and gold links, for 81 more states of the register: from Ur, Lagash and the Old Kingdom of Egypt to the Qin, Sui and Northern Wei, the Huns, Hephthalites and Uyghurs, Phrygia, Colchis and Artaxiad Armenia, the Visigoths, Vandals and Great Moravia, the Aghlabids, Idrisids, Marinids and Zengids, Funan, Chenla, Champa, Medang and Malacca, Ife, Dagbon, Loango, Ifat and Alodia, Saint-Domingue, Colonial Brazil, the Republic of Texas and the Confederacy, and the modern republics from Hungary and Turkey to Rwanda, Singapore and East Timor.

item.title: Two new essays: Before the State, and How Songs Travel
item.guid: 2026-11-02 Two new essays: Before the State, and How Songs Travel
item.description: Research Series 07 asks how peoples lived without kings, from the Natufians and the Jōmon to the five living cultures that have outlived the states around them; 08 follows the 300 songs of Songs in History from the oldest tablets to the anthems, the tunes that branched into other nations' songs, and what states and movements made of them. Also new in Songs in History: Chollima on the Wing, the song of North Korea's Chollima Movement, and an entry for the movement itself.

item.title: Songs of states and causes, and a dozen new features
item.guid: 2026-11-02 Songs of states and causes, and a dozen new features
item.description: Sixty-six songs of states, parties and causes join Songs in History, from Rule, Britannia! and the Soviet anthem to the songs of Mao's China, North Korea, fascist Italy and the Hong Kong protests, each told as history. New: compare any two profiles side by side; a timeline view of the profiles; Where Is This Song From?, a daily song game; Born on This Day on the home page; Next to read; search inside the songs' words; the encyclopedia filtered by era and by picture; levels in My Passport; an On This Day card for other websites; reading paths read aloud as a guided tour; this What's new page; worksheets on the cultures and the songs; and the Epic of Gilgamesh now in Sumerian.

item.title: Encyclopedia, offline reading, Meanwhile in the world
item.guid: 2026-11-02 Encyclopedia, offline reading, Meanwhile in the world
item.description: 229 songs and 16 forms of government have entries of their own; entries and songs show what else was happening in the world that year; the home page has a Song of the Day; pages already read open without a connection, and the site can be added to a phone's home screen.

item.title: Thirty new cultures
item.description: The culture archive grows from 15 to 45, with more of Asia and South Asia: Mehrgarh, the Vedic civilisation, Sangam-age Tamilakam, Jōmon, Yayoi, Liangzhu, Sanxingdui, Dong Son, the Ainu and more, from the Natufians and the Yamnaya to the Taíno, the Thule people and the Māori.

item.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh, and better performances
item.guid: 2026-11-02 The Epic of Gilgamesh, and better performances
item.description: The Epic of Gilgamesh joins Songs in History with Peter Pringle's performance in Sumerian; eight songs have a better recording.

item.title: Songs in History
item.description: 233 songs handed down through history, from a Sumerian hymn to songs of the Cold War: their story, their words in the original, romanized and in English where they are in the public domain, and a sung performance.

item.title: Forms of government
item.description: Twenty forms of government, from absolute monarchy to the city-state and colonial rule, each with how it works, its history, its strengths and weaknesses; a hub that compares them and lets you design a state; and an essay, Who Should Rule?

item.title: The inventions tree
item.description: 218 inventions and discoveries in eleven lanes, from stone tools to the World Wide Web: what each built on, what it led to and who made it first.

item.title: Social ladders
item.description: How thirty societies ranked their people, ruler to enslaved, with how many stood on each rung; be born into one by chance, compare two, or put the ranks in order in a game.

item.title: Thirty cultures and movements, speeches and paths
item.guid: 2026-10-29 Thirty cultures and movements, speeches and paths
item.description: The first cultures and movements, 138 new encyclopedia entries, twenty more great speeches and ten more reading paths.

item.title: Rise and Fall Race, Flashcards, Who Said It?
item.guid: 2026-10-28 Rise and Fall Race, Flashcards, Who Said It?
item.description: Race empires through the centuries, learn with flashcards, guess who said a quotation, test yourself at the end of a profile, and see everything you have read on My timeline.
